title: Normalized completed open, scalar and quotient tower constructions
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be the adic datum with completed coefficient sheaves $A_V$ and strict reduction tower $K_\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the exact localized ringed-site open adjunction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], constructed by extension presheaves [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Write $j_!$ for its completed-module realization, and normalize its right adjoint as module inverse image along the completed coefficient identification of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and [def-weil-pbc-four-corners], so that $j^*$ is the exact strict-tower pullback of [def-weil-pbc-exact-pullback-interface]. Define $J_j$ by applying $j_!$ to the entire strict tower and descending exactly to the unbounded derived category; its adjunction $J_j\dashv j^*$ is the derived ordinary adjunction. Write $r_V$ for restriction of scalars along $\underline A_V\to A_V$ [def-cbc-completed-scalar-pullback-interface], and use the constant-$A$ open adjunction of [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Define $e_j:r_TJ_j\simeq J_jr_U$ as the inverse of the mate of the ordinary scalar/pullback comparison [def-weil-pbc-ring-restriction-pullback-comparison] over the constant-coefficient identifications of [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations]; equivalently it is the identity on the underlying extension presheaves, sheafified and then descended termwise. For arbitrary $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))$, define $q_{j,K}:(j_!K)_\bullet\simeq J_jK_\bullet$ as the inverse of the completed open transpose of the reduction of the open unit followed by the inverse normalized reduction/pullback comparison of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The named invertibility properties give these specified inverses; they are not arbitrary isomorphisms. Define the quotient/open/scalar comparison to be $r_T(q_{j,K})$ followed by $e_{j,K_\bullet}$. All termwise constructions retain every quotient transition. The ordinary scalar/open mate is invertible, and the inverse quotient/open transpose is natural in $K$ and invertible. No completeness or cohomological bound is assumed.
